$comment: The journal app (ADR 0011) as tests at the `jellymoon` binary's boundary, in priority order. A building session changes ONLY the `passes` field, and sets it true only after `test` passes locally and in CI. Never delete, reword or reorder a feature to make it pass; a feature that turns out wrong gets a new feature plus a note in progress/. `blockedBy` names what must happen before work starts. This list was rewritten once, at the restart (ADR 0012). See docs/development/workflow.md.

features.description: Jellymoon collects one local day of what a person typed to Claude Code, and nothing else
steps: `jellymoon day --date <day> --logs <dir>` prints that day's turns as JSON: the time, the project, the person's text and the agent's last reply in the same turn, cut short
a turn is kept only when the log marks it as typed by a person; tool results, task notices, compaction summaries, sidechains and prompts sent by other programs are left out
text shaped like a credential is replaced before it is printed, in the person's text and in the reply
a folder the person switched off with --skip contributes no turns
the day is the local calendar day: a turn typed at 23:59 and one typed at 00:01 land on different days
a log line that is not valid JSON is skipped and the rest of the file is still read

features.description: One reading call turns a day into page data, and code refuses what the person did not say
steps: page data is a typed shape in core with example files that round-trip: wishes (label, said, project, state, stars) and clashes
`jellymoon page --date <day>` sends the day to the harness in one headless call with every tool, MCP server and saved session turned off, asserted on the command line the fake harness receives
a wish whose `said` is not an exact substring of what the person typed that day is dropped, and so is a clash that quotes words the person did not type
output that is not valid page data gives an error and no page; more than 8 wishes are cut to 8
no text in the day can add a tool or a flag to the call

features.description: The app draws a page from page data using only the kit
steps: the app's layout command reads page data and prints every placed piece: its kind, position and size
every wish gets one little one and one star per finished job; a let-go wish is drawn greyed; a clash gets one note with both quotes
no two labels overlap on a page of 8 wishes with the longest allowed labels
text from page data is drawn as text only; markup or control characters in a label change nothing but the label
a kind the kit does not have falls back to a plain note

features.description: A ruling made on a page reaches a running Claude Code session once, at its next step
steps: installing the hook adds one entry to the harness settings and leaves every other byte as it was; uninstalling restores the file exactly
with no ruling waiting the hook prints nothing and exits 0
a ruling is handed to each running session exactly once, as the person's newer decision
a real Claude Code turn told to do one thing, then sent a ruling to do another, does the other (harness-real)

features.description: Holding a key and saying a wish starts an agent on it
steps: a wish made in the app appears on today's page at once, in the person's exact words, in the working state
Jellymoon starts a run for it with the person's harness (ADR 0011, sections 5 and 7) and the wish's star appears when the run reports it finished
a wish made while no harness is installed stays on the page and says why nothing started

features.description: Jellymoon collects a day of what a person typed to Codex the same way
steps: `jellymoon day` reads Codex session logs with the same output shape and the same rules as F26
sessions another program drove through ACP contribute no turns
blockedBy: a typed Codex session to build the fixture from

features.description: A theme changes how a page looks and nothing else
steps: the same page data laid out under the sticker theme and the plain theme places the same pieces in the same order
the plain theme has no tilt and no idle motion
a theme file with an unknown key or a missing piece falls back to the default for that piece
a theme carries no code: a theme file containing a script or a path outside its folder is refused

features.description: One command installs Jellymoon on a Mac with no Apple Developer signature
steps: the install script downloads the release for the machine's architecture, checks its checksum, and puts the app and the `jellymoon` binary in the user's own folders with no sudo
the app opens with no Gatekeeper block because the download is not quarantined
running it again updates in place
an uninstall command removes everything it added and the delivery hook

features.description: Opening the app shows today's page
steps: `jellymoon-app` with no `--page` shows a waiting page drawn by the kit at once, reads the day off the window's thread by calling core's `day` and `page` (never by running the `jellymoon` binary), and shows the page when it is ready; `layout` with no `--page` prints that page, and `layout --waiting` the waiting page

the page data of each day is kept in the user's jellymoon folder; opening again shows the kept page and makes a reading call only when the day's count of turns differs from the count the kept page was read from, or with `--fresh`; `--date` shows another day

when the reading cannot run (no harness, the call fails, the reply is not page data, no session logs) the page is one plain note that says why in plain words, on the kept page when there is one; a day with nothing typed says so and makes no call
only what core's `day` returns goes to the reading call, with every tool off; what is kept is the checked page data and nothing else; nothing from the day is printed

features.description: A tap on a clash settles it, and the ruling reaches the person's running sessions
steps: a tap on one of a clash's two options makes one ruling by calling core's `rule` (never by running the `jellymoon` binary): the option tapped stands and the other is what it replaces, both being that clash's statements in the day's page data; `jellymoon-app tap --clash <n> --option <k>` does the same on the kept page and prints the ruling as JSON, and `jellymoon hook` then tells a session that ruling once

the page shows the clash settled at once, the statement that stands as text and the replaced one struck, with no reading; it stays settled when the app is opened again; a tap on the struck statement makes a new ruling the other way round, and a tap on the one that already stands makes none

a tap on a clash never changes Claude Code's settings; while the hook is not installed a page with a clash carries one note with one option, `Turn on delivery`, whose tap (`tap --delivery-on`) installs core's hook for the installed `jellymoon` command; when that command is not found the note says how to do it from a terminal; when the hook is installed the note is gone

a tap on a clash that is not on the kept page, an option out of range or a day with no kept page is refused in one line and writes nothing; the only text a tap can put into a ruling is the two statements of the page data, through core's cleaning, also when the kept page was changed after the reading

features.description: The tap's rules live in core and are proved at the `jellymoon` command
steps: `jellymoon settle --date <day> --clash <n> --option <1|2>` is the tap: it makes one ruling of that clash's two statements from the day's kept page by core's `settle`, prints `{ruling, stands, replaces, unkept}` as one line of JSON, and `jellymoon hook` then tells a session that ruling once; the app's window calls the same core function and `jellymoon-app` has no `tap` command

a tap on the statement that stands makes no ruling, read from the waiting rulings as well as the settlement; a ruling whose settlement could not be written exits 0 with the ruling and the reason, and the same tap again makes no second ruling; two taps at once on two clashes both keep theirs

the kept page is used only as a plain file of the day asked for that neither group nor others can write to; a settlement of another day, of another shape, with an unknown field or over 64 KiB says nothing about what stands; what a tap writes is 0600 in folders set to 0700; every refusal is one line and writes nothing

`jellymoon hook install --installed` installs the hook only for an installed `jellymoon` command that is a regular, runnable, non-empty file only its owner can write to, in a folder not everyone can write to, by an absolute path, with a link followed and its target checked; a relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is refused by every `hook install`

features.description: A typed wish is kept on today's page in the person's exact words
steps: `jellymoon wish --say <words> --project <name>` keeps a made wish for today in the working state, in the person's exact words after core's cleaning, and prints `{wish: {id, said, project, state, stars}, run: null, why}` as one line of JSON

the page draws the made wish with no reading call: `jellymoon page` for a kept day and the app's today show it with the reading's wishes, under an id the reading can never give, and a reading that rewrites the kept page does not lose it
with no run, `why` says in fixed words that nothing was started
a wish that is empty once cleaned, too long, one too many for the day, or for a project name that is not one plain name is refused in one line and writes nothing

features.description: A run gets its own copy of the repo
steps: `jellymoon copy make` gives a run a git worktree of the person's repo on a branch of its own and prints `{run, folder, branch, kept}` as one line of JSON; the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged

`jellymoon copy clean` removes only a folder directly inside the copies' own root, runs no hook and reads no file from the run's folder: a run id of `..`, a link inside the root, a rewritten `.git` file and a repo with `post-checkout` and `fsmonitor` set leave everything outside byte for byte as it was, and a marker file is never written
a failed run's copy is kept, the newest five only

features.description: A wish starts a run with the person's harness, and its star appears when the run reports it finished
steps: `jellymoon run --wish <id>` starts the person's harness headless in the run's copy and prints `{run, wish, outcome, star, denied, why}` as one line of JSON, `outcome` being `completed`, `failed` or `not_started`

the harness gets only the allow-listed environment (`PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `USER`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TERM`) and the arguments that fix what the run may do: a planted token variable is absent, and the person's allow rules, MCP servers and project hooks are shut out
a result that is a success with exit 0 adds one star, in fixed words, to the wish; after the run the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged and only the run's branch is new
with no harness the wish stays and `why` names the places looked; a project name that matches two folders is refused with nothing written

features.description: A run can be stopped, and nothing it asks for is allowed unless listed
steps: `jellymoon run stop` interrupts the run, then signals it, then kills it, and the outcome is `cancelled`; an agent deaf to the interrupt and to the signal is gone all the same
what the agent asks for outside its list is denied and counted in `denied`, never allowed
a stopped run keeps its copy

features.description: A wish made with `--run` starts its own run, which outlives the command that asked for it
steps: `jellymoon wish --say <words> --project <name> --run` keeps the wish, starts `jellymoon run` for it as a process of its own, prints `{wish, run, why}` with the run's id once the wish names it, and exits while the run goes; `jellymoon page` then shows the wish working, and done with its star when the run completes
a run that could not be started leaves the wish kept and exits 0: with no harness, two folders of the name, or a folder that is no repo's top, `run` is null and `why` is core's own line

a folder found in a session log that is not the person's own is refused, a folder switched off with `--skip` is not found, and a fourth run while three are going is refused, each in one line with no copy made

features.description: A wish typed in the app's window is on today's page at once, and its run starts
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` prints one `entry` piece on a day's page, with one option per project of the day's reading; a day with no project read prints none

words entered for a project are kept by core's `wish` and drawn at once in the working state with no reading; the run is started by core's `run_apart` with the checked installed `jellymoon` command, never in the app's own process, and the page shows the star when it completes, with no tap and no reopening
words core refuses, a command that is not found, and a run that was not started each leave one plain note that says why in core's words; a refused wish writes nothing
the kit's entry keeps text being composed apart from text entered: Enter during a composition enters nothing

features.description: A tap on a working made wish stops its run
steps: a tap on the character of a made wish whose run is going shows one choice, `Stop it`; its tap calls core's `stop_run` off the window's thread, and the page says the run is being stopped, then draws the wish as needing the person with no star
a tap on any other character, on a wish with no run going, or on a stop choice whose run has ended meanwhile stops nothing and writes nothing

features.description: A finished run's work is shown as what it made, with no git and no folder
steps: `jellymoon run show --wish <id>` prints one line of JSON for a made wish whose run completed: the run, the wish, whether the work waits, was kept or was tossed, and its files, each with a cleaned name, whether it was made, changed or removed, its size, whether it is text, a link or another repo's entry, and whether it is one the person's tools obey (ADR 0017, decision 6); the list is cut at a stated count and says how many more there are

`--file <n>` prints that file as it is in the work, the whole text and never a diff, cleaned at the door every kept text is cleaned at and cut at a stated size; a file that is not text, a link, or a number that names no file prints a refusal in fixed words and no bytes of the file

everything is read from the repo's store by the run's commit and its parent: the person's working tree, `HEAD`, index and refs are unchanged, no file of the work is written to disk, opened or run, and a file name that looks like an option or holds control characters reaches git and the page only as data
a wish with no run, a run that is going, failed or was cancelled, a record that cannot be read, and a repo that is gone each print one plain refusal and exit 1

features.description: Keeping a run's work lands it on the branch the person stands on, as one commit by them
steps: `jellymoon run keep --wish <id>` with the checkout where the run started moves the person's branch forward to the run's commit; with commits of the person's own since, it lands one new commit on top of theirs that holds both; either way the files are in their working tree, the run's branch is gone, the record says `kept` with the commit, and it prints `{run, wish, kept, onto, why}`

work that no longer fits is refused with the working tree, `HEAD`, index and every ref unchanged and the reason in fixed words: the same lines changed on both sides, an unsaved change or an untracked file of the person's in the way, no branch stood on, a rebase, merge, cherry-pick or bisect in progress, a history that no longer holds the run's start, or a git too old to merge in the store

work that adds or changes a submodule entry or `.gitmodules` is never kept; work that touches a file the person's tools obey is refused unless `--with-settings` is given; no hook of the repo runs, nothing is fetched and nothing is pushed
`--ask` prints what a keep would do or why it would be refused, and changes nothing
a keep cut off at any of its steps is finished or begun again by the next `run keep`, and the work never lands twice; a second keep, and a keep of tossed work, change nothing and say so

features.description: Tossing a run's work removes its branch and lets the wish go
steps: `jellymoon run toss --wish <id>` on work that waits writes `tossed` and the commit's id in the run's record, then deletes the run's branch as the run's own ref at that commit, and the wish is drawn `let go`; it prints `{run, wish, tossed, commit, why}`

the branch is left and nothing is written when someone stands on it, when it is a symbolic ref, or when it moved since the work was shown; no other branch, tag or ref changes, and the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged
a toss of a failed or cancelled run removes its kept copy as `copy clean` does, and its branch by the same rule
a second toss, and a toss of kept work, change nothing and say so

features.description: A tap on a little one opens its wish, and work that waits is shown, kept or tossed there
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` prints, for a made wish whose work waits, one note with the wish's own words, how many files the work made, changed and removed with their names, and three choices: `Show me`, `Keep it`, `Toss it`; core says which wishes those are
`Show me` draws one file of the work as text in the window, by core's `run show`; nothing is handed to the system's opener

`Keep it` and `Toss it` call core off the window's thread and draw core's words: the wish stays done with its star and the note goes, or the wish is drawn let go; a refused keep leaves one plain note with core's reason, and work that touches files the person's tools obey names them and asks once more before it is kept
a tap on any other little one shows its wish's own words and state, and changes nothing
